newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products down,but cautious over Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products down,but cautious over Iraq.

text.p: Singapore oil products were generally weaker as the market corrected itself further following the knee-jerk jump earlier this week on news of the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq, traders said.

Prices also came off in line with lower crude values as tension eased in the Middle East, but traders remained cautious. But further big cuts are not expected as the market is fairly well supported at the these levels due to low crude and oil product stocks in the west, one trader said.
Fuel oil softened with a 180-centistoke cargo for lifting Sept 20-25 done between two majors at $111.50, down $1.50.

Gas oil swaps eased by 40 cents Thursday with swap trades for October seen at $26.70, down from Wednesday's trades at $27.10, brokers said.Physical buyers remained cautious and bids were seen at $26.60, or close to prevailing swap prices, traders said. Producers in Singapore have sold gas oil earlier this week at a premium of about 40 cents above Singapore spot quotes, one refiner said. Jet fuel edged down and a refiner sold 200,000 barrels to a European major at $29.90 for lifting Sept 28-Oct 2.
Naphtha stabilised after Wednesday's plunge on the back of steady Japanese open-spec levels. Singapore September paper was down slightly at $20.25-$20.55.

Naphtha sentiment was bearish as October demand from north Asian is down due to petrochemical shutdowns while ample Indian supplies were seen in September. Traders said Indian cargoes would have to head to the west instead where prices were holding well. Light distillate stocks rose by more than half a million barrels to 5.234 million barrels, putting pressure on gasoline. Trades were reported at low levels of $22.15 per barrel for 95-octane unleaded, $23.35 for 97-octane and $22.15 for 92-octane for end September/early October lifting.
